lines.t: This horse could do maths. Ask him three plus two... and he taps his hoof five times.
His owner was a maths teacher. He spent years teaching the horse numbers, words, even the calendar.
Crowds came every day to see Clever Hans.
A horse? Doing maths? Next you'll tell me he pays taxes.
The teacher just smiled. Ask him yourself.
So the experts came. Thirteen of them. A vet, a circus boss, an army officer, and teachers.
They looked for strings. Secret signals. Tricks. Nothing.
Fine. Then a stranger asks the questions.
The owner left. A stranger asked... and Hans still got it right!
The experts gave up. No trick, they said.
Then one young scientist tried something tiny. He asked a question that he did not know the answer to.
And Hans kept tapping. Six. Seven. Eight. Nine. He had no idea.
You see, when you ask Hans a question, you watch his hoof. As he gets close to the answer, you tense up. When he hits it, your head lifts. Just a tiny bit.
Hans saw it every time. That was his signal to stop.
When he could see the person, he was right almost nine times out of ten. With blinders on? Almost never.
Hans never knew any maths. He was reading the faces of the smartest people in the city. And not one of them noticed.
Could Hans read you? A, easily. Or B, no way.
